title.narrative: Harmonizing the classification of goods based on WCO standards to enhance African trade

description.narrative: This action is part of the External Investment Plan and aims to assist African national customs administrations, regional economic communities and relevant stakeholders, including the African Union Commission, in the coordinated implementation and uniform application of the Harmonized System of the World Customs Organization (WCO). Key aims are, among others, to contribute to the establishment of the African Continental Free Trade Area (CFTA) as envisaged by the African Union (AU), to increase intra-African trade and trade between Africa and the European Union, to facilitate the implementation of Economic Partnership Agreements (EPAs), Association Agreements (AAs) and Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Agreements (DCFTAs), and develop trade with the rest of the world, thus contributing more generally to the implementation of the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement. This should be achieved by supporting Customs reform and modernization and implementation of international standards and best practices developed by the WCO, particularly the Harmonized System (HS) for the classification of traded goods, as well as related provisions of the WTO Agreement on Trade Facilitation (TFA) and the Revised Kyoto Convention (RKC) of the WCO.
